findings.claim: 23.02.02's Happy Path — the only place in the domain that enumerates a deduction category vocabulary — specifies a UK sole-trader jurisdiction, while the same file's resolved Q-01 and the parent index's resolved Q-01 lock v1 to US rules only, and the file's own D-02 requires an unsupported jurisdiction to be refused rather than served.
findings.evidence: 23.02.02-deduction-categorization-jurisdiction-rules.md:27-28 — "1. Musician declares UK sole-trader jurisdiction. | 2. Their capture surface offers a UK-shaped vocabulary: equipment, instruments, rehearsal, travel, subsistence, home-studio use, professional fees." Contradicted by 23.02.02:83 — "~~Which jurisdictions at launch~~ is **RESOLVED — the United States only** … so v1 encodes US musician/sole-trader rules alone" and by 23.02-expenses-tax-readiness-index.md:48 — "**RESOLVED — the United States only.** … v1 encodes US sole-trader (Schedule C) rules and nothing else". Also contradicted by the same file's D-02 (23.02.02:76) — "Unsupported jurisdictions fail honestly rather than degrading to a generic list" and its Edge Case (23.02.02:38) — "Jurisdiction not supported | Must fail honestly … Explicit 'not supported; export raw data instead'". Under the locked scope, the Happy Path describes a flow v1 must refuse.
findings.forcedInvention: The entire v1 category vocabulary. CX-01 (23.02-expenses-tax-readiness-cx.md:10,21) states that the jurisdiction rule set "**defines** the category vocabulary available at capture; capture cannot offer a neutral category list" and that "capture **cannot ship jurisdiction-neutral**" — so an implementer must invent the US Schedule C vocabulary, its apportionment rules and its capital threshold from scratch, because the only worked example given is out of scope. Two implementers would build different category enums, and one of them may build the UK list the Happy Path actually specifies.
findings.twoImplementerTest: FAILS. One implementer follows the Happy Path and ships the seven UK categories; another follows Q-01/D-02 and ships Schedule C categories while refusing UK declarations outright.

findings.claim: 23.05.02 requires a public, Fan-readable, year-grouped milestone timeline as first-class behaviour, while the resolution of its own Q-01 (and of the parent's Q-03) binds any public projection to 01.06.02 D-06, which forbids rendering a timeline spine or per-year chronological density on any public surface. Both statements are normative and neither carries a marker.
findings.evidence: Required: 23.05.02-auto-milestone-timeline.md:23-24 — "Each milestone has a private form (complete, factual) and a **public projection** (curated, artist-controlled). The two are one entity with a visibility rule"; :30 — "The Musician toggles it public; it joins their artist profile story (01/20)"; :19 (Fan Role Lens) — "An artist's public timeline is fan-facing content — the story of the act. They see the public projection"; :52 (Populated state) — "Chronological, grouped by year, with public/private markers"; and career-finance-business-index.md:97-99 — Fan "holds exactly one cell in the entire domain: `👁️ Read-only` on 23.05, and only on the *public projection* of the milestone timeline (23.05.02)". Forbidden: 23.05.02:85 — "**RESOLVED — it stays in 23** … and any public projection is bound by `01.06.02` D-06", where 01.06.02-credit-backed-portfolio.md:215 D-06 reads "never renders chronological density on a public surface — no activity graph, no per-year counts, **no timeline spine**. A range is a fact; a timeline invites gap-reading" and 01.06.02:106 generalises it — "**no chronological density on any public surface**". Same rule restated as an absolute prohibition at 01.06.02:68 — "Per-year credit density / activity timeline | ❌ **Never**".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the public artist timeline exists at all, and if it does, what form of it survives D-06 (a range? a set of undated markers? a curated subset with no chronology?). The domain's single Fan-facing surface, its visibility model, and the D-06 exception boundary all have to be invented.
findings.twoImplementerTest: FAILS. One implementer builds the year-grouped public timeline the feature and the domain Role Matrix describe; another refuses to render any public chronology and drops the Fan cell entirely, per the constraint the same file says binds it.

findings.claim: 23.07.03 enumerates the band distribution rule's permitted shapes twice, with different members, both times as a closed set — its Behavior says Equal / Weighted / Per-role, while its own resolved Q-02 and the parent's resolved Q-03 say the shapes are fixed by 01.04.03 as equal / by income share / manual per event.
findings.evidence: 23.07.03-band-treasury-member-distribution.md:29-32 — "**Remainder divides by the distribution rule** — one of three shapes agreed by the band … - **Equal** — remainder ÷ N members. - **Weighted** — fixed percentages per member summing to 100%. - **Per-role** — shares keyed to role/contribution (e.g. touring members vs. writers), still summing to 100%." Contradicted by 23.07.03:102 — "The rule's shapes are fixed by [01.04.03] Behavior: 'exactly three shapes: **equal** (split N ways), **by income share** (the percentages fixed in 01.04.01), or **manual per event**'", and by the parent's resolution at 23.07-budgeting-project-tour-pl-index.md:48 — "01.04.03 Treasury Mandate's Behavior fixes the resulting rule to 'exactly three shapes: **equal** (split N ways), **by income share** (the percentages fixed in 01.04.01), or **manual per event**'". 'Per-role' and 'manual per event' are different objects: one is a standing rule keyed to role, the other is an ad-hoc per-distribution entry. Both enumerations are stated as exhaustive ('one of three shapes' / 'exactly three shapes').
findings.forcedInvention: The distribution-rule enum itself — the load-bearing input to the waterfall that pays real money to real people. An implementer must decide whether a standing per-role rule exists, whether manual-per-event is permitted, and which of the two documents governs.
findings.twoImplementerTest: FAILS. One implementer ships a role-weighted standing rule and no per-event override; another ships a per-event manual path and no role dimension. The two produce different payments from identical facts.

findings.claim: Adjacent sections of the same CX file disagree about whether an unconfirmed extracted term may drive an alert: CX-01 makes confirmation mandatory before an alert, CX-02 requires the alert to fire regardless.
findings.evidence: 23.04-deal-contract-vault-cx.md:31 (CX-01 §2) — "Upload → extract → user confirms each term. **Confirmation is mandatory, not optional**: an unconfirmed extraction must never silently drive an alert or a reconciliation finding." Versus 23.04-deal-contract-vault-cx.md:51 (CX-02 §5) — "A date passing while the extraction is still unconfirmed — **the alert must fire anyway, flagged as unconfirmed**. Silence is the one unacceptable outcome." The feature that owns alerts settles it in favour of firing (23.04.03-option-reversion-obligation-alerts.md:86 D-02 — "Unconfirmed dates alert anyway, flagged"; :45,:61 same), and 23.04.02's Behavior constrains only reconciliation ("Unconfirmed extractions are visibly provisional and must never silently drive a reconciliation finding", 23.04.02:23) — so the CX-01 sentence is the outlier and its 'alert' clause is wrong.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the alert scheduler has a confirmation gate. Kept at warning rather than blocking because CX-01's qualifier 'silently' admits a reconciling reading (a flagged alert is not silent) and because the owning feature's D-02 resolves the direction — but a spec writer working from the CX file alone would build the gate.
findings.twoImplementerTest: MARGINAL. A reader of the CX file builds a confirmation gate; a reader of 23.04.03 does not. The consequence — a missed reversion — is the catastrophic failure the sub-domain exists to prevent (23.04.03:44).

findings.claim: 23.07.03's Edge Cases still pose the no-distribution-rule case as an open parent question and assert that nothing can be computed, while the same file's Q-02 and the parent's Q-03 are both resolved and state that an equal-shares legal default already governs the band and is disclosed to them.
findings.evidence: 23.07.03-band-treasury-member-distribution.md:49 — "**No distribution rule exists** | The overwhelming majority of bands. **Nothing can be computed** | Parent Q-03: does the platform ask them to agree one … or refuse to guess?" But 23.07.03:102 — "✅ **RESOLVED** — it discloses the default that already governs them rather than prompting a negotiation … the legal default being an equal-shares general partnership", and 23.07-budgeting-project-tour-pl-index.md:48 — "✅ **RESOLVED — neither: it discloses the default that already governs them, and it never guesses." The unresolved residue is substantive rather than cosmetic: disclosure of an equal-shares default is not the same as computing a distribution from it, and the Empty state ('a band with no agreed rule is the normal starting condition, not an error', 23.07.03:64) does not say which behaviour applies.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the waterfall computes a provisional equal-shares distribution when no rule has been captured, or blocks at step 3. Given that this is the majority case for bands, the choice determines whether the feature functions for most of its users.
findings.twoImplementerTest: FAILS on the computability question. One implementer blocks distribution until a rule is captured; another computes equal shares from the disclosed legal default.

findings.claim: Three Operator cells in the domain Role Matrix are more restrictive than the per-child matrices they summarise, and no aggregation rule is stated — the same role gets two different access levels for the same feature depending on which document is read.
findings.evidence: career-finance-business-index.md:75 gives Operator `📊 Reports` for all of 23.02, but 23.02-expenses-tax-readiness-index.md:27 gives Operator `✅ Full` on 23.02.01 Expense & Receipt Capture (and 23.02.01:18 confirms it: "Operator | Full | Rent, PRS/PPL-class licences, staff, backline repair, bar stock"). career-finance-business-index.md:77 gives Operator `👁️ Read-only` for all of 23.04, but 23.04-deal-contract-vault-index.md:27 gives Operator `✅ Full` on 23.04.01 Contract Vault (and 23.04.01:18 confirms it). career-finance-business-index.md:80 gives Operator `📊 Reports` for all of 23.07, but 23.07-budgeting-project-tour-pl-index.md:26 gives Operator `✅ Full` on 23.07.01. The aggregation is also inconsistent in direction: the Fan cell for 23.05 takes the most permissive child value (`👁️` from 23.05.02, per career-finance-business-index.md:97-99) while the Operator cells take neither the maximum nor the minimum of their children.

Mitigated but not resolved by the precedence hint at career-finance-business-index.md:104 ("Per-role behavioural detail lives in each feature file's **Role Lens**"), which governs behavioural detail rather than access levels — and the domain matrix's reading note argues substantively from its own cells ("`📊 Reports` where their business is company-shaped", :91-92), so it does not read as a lossy summary.

findings.claim: The feature's primary privacy control is asserted as a hard rule with no value, and the related dimensionality limit is left open with no owner and a spent deferral target — so the control that decides whether the feature is safe cannot be implemented as specified.
findings.evidence: 23.05.03-peer-cohort-benchmarking.md:80 D-03 — "**Hard minimum cohort size, enforced; show nothing below it**" with no number anywhere in the file; :37 — "Hard minimum cohort size, enforced. Show nothing rather than something. This is a privacy control, not a UX preference"; :23 — "Benchmarks are **aggregates with a minimum cohort size**, below which nothing is shown at all". The dimensionality half is an untracked PENDING: :43 — "Rates differ by genre, city, client type, union status | A single benchmark is meaningless across those splits | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — **how many dimensions before the cohort is too small to show?**" — no owner, and the named stage has completed (ideation-index.md records Step 5 complete and the MoSCoW ledger places all three 23.05 features). Neither of the file's three Open Questions covers the threshold value.
findings.forcedInvention: The k-anonymity value and the cohort dimension budget. The file itself supplies the failure it prevents — "Four session drummers in one city is four named people; one of them can work out the others' rates" (:37) — which makes the missing number a re-identification risk rather than a tuning parameter.
findings.twoImplementerTest: FAILS. k=3 and k=25 are both defensible readings of 'hard minimum' and produce materially different products — one of which leaks rates.

findings.claim: The out-of-order delivery rule depends on a 'reconciliation window' that is never given a value and is not covered by any open question, while the file's sibling threshold (auto-merge confidence) is explicitly tracked.
findings.evidence: 23.01.01-income-event-ledger.md:46 — "The reversing or projecting record is parked as pending, keyed to the missing original's idempotency key, and reconciled when the original lands; if the original never arrives **within the reconciliation window**, the orphan is surfaced for review rather than silently applied or dropped." Restated as a decision without a value at :99 D-06 — "Out-of-order records are parked and reconciled, never applied or dropped". By contrast the file does track its other threshold: :108 Q-04 — "For the reconciliation confidence threshold (D-04), what is the auto-merge vs ask boundary … | Agent | `/write-be-spec`" — so the omission is asymmetric rather than a deliberate deferral pattern.
findings.forcedInvention: How long an orphaned reversal or FX projection is held before it becomes a review item. The user-visible consequence is specified ('The affected total shows an "N records pending reconciliation" marker'), so the window determines when a financial total stops carrying a caveat.
findings.twoImplementerTest: FAILS on timing. 24 hours, 30 days and 'never expire' are all consistent with the text and produce visibly different ledgers.

findings.claim: The import feature's core ingestion path — how an arbitrary bank CSV is mapped — is left unresolved by an owner-less marker whose deferral stage has already completed, and no open question in the file or its parent covers it.
findings.evidence: 23.01.02-off-platform-income-import.md:44 — "CSV format unrecognized (every bank differs) | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — **column-mapping UI vs per-bank parsers is unresolved** | Mapping step". The marker carries no owner, and the named stage has closed (23.01.02's own Q-01/Q-02 rows state "`/ideate-validate` has run and closed", and the feature is a Should at `[PARTIAL]`, i.e. Step 5 Level-1 complete). The file's three Open Questions cover bank linking, evidence adjudication and financial-data-processor scope — none covers format handling. The States table presumes a resolution exists: "Error | Parse failed / unmappable columns | Row-level errors — never reject a whole file for one bad row" (:56).
findings.forcedInvention: The entire import ingestion model — a generic user-driven column mapper versus a maintained set of per-bank parsers. These are different products with different cold-start behaviour, different failure modes and different ongoing maintenance obligations, and the choice interacts with the (tracked) bank-linking question.

findings.unit: 23-career-finance-business (domain root — pattern spanning five sub-domain CX files)
findings.claim: The notification-fan-out synthesis question is deferred in five sub-domain CX files by an identical marker that carries no owner and names a deferral stage that has already completed, so no stage owns the notification design for those cross-cuts.
findings.evidence: Five occurrences, all reading "Deferred — `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`" with no owner: 23.01-income-aggregation-financial-identity-cx.md:67 (CX-03 §4, credit revoked while earnings display); 23.02-expenses-tax-readiness-cx.md:33 (CX-01 §4, delegate re-categorisation); 23.04-deal-contract-vault-cx.md:33 (CX-01 §4, extraction confirmation); 23.05-career-progression-benchmarking-cx.md:61 (CX-03 §4, cohort membership change); 23.06-advances-commission-recoupment-cx.md:69 (CX-03 §5, netting-to-runway state transition). The named stage is closed — ideation-index.md:65-67 records Step 5 complete for all Musts/Shoulds and Coulds/Won'ts as correctly out of scope, and :77 records all 24 domain CX files at `[DEEP]`. The other four synthesis questions in each of those cross-cuts are answered, so these are omissions inside otherwise-complete sections rather than a documented scope boundary.
findings.forcedInvention: Who gets notified, and whether at all, when a credit is revoked against displayed earnings, when a delegate re-categorises a row, when an extraction is confirmed, when cohort membership shifts under a user, and when a netting change moves a runway. Reported once as a pattern rather than five times because the defect and the fix are identical in each file.
findings.twoImplementerTest: PARTIAL. Each individual gap is small; the pattern leaves five cross-cut notification behaviours unowned after the stage that was supposed to own them has closed.

findings.claim: Band-level goals are deferred by an owner-less marker to a completed stage, leaving the object model for goals — whose goals, over whose activity — unspecified in a sub-domain whose entire design rests on goals being queries over activity.
findings.evidence: 23.05.01-career-goals-roadmap-templates.md:42 — "Band-level goals | The band's goals vs the member's are different objects (01) | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`". No owner; the stage is closed. The file's three Open Questions cover declared-vs-verified counting (resolved), MoSCoW survival (resolved) and notification tone — none covers the entity dimension. The rest of the domain treats band-versus-person as load-bearing and specifies it explicitly elsewhere (23.01.01:41, 23.07.03 passim), so silence here is inconsistent rather than deliberate.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a Band entity can hold goals, and if so whether a member's goal may derive over band activity — which decides what the goal derivation query joins on.
findings.twoImplementerTest: FAILS. One implementer scopes goals to a person only; another adds an entity dimension to every goal derivation.

notableStrengths: 23.01.01 is the strongest unit in the domain: forged-event rejection, tier immutability from every user-facing path, propose-don't-auto-merge reconciliation, parked out-of-order records, and an explicit refusal to render a partial financial total are all specified with the failure each prevents.

The domain-wide invariants (INV-01..05, career-finance-business-cx.md:171-177) are derived from three or more independent occurrences each and are cited by the features that depend on them, which removes a large class of cross-feature ambiguity that would otherwise have to be rediscovered per feature.

Refusal-to-compute is specified as a first-class behaviour with named blockers rather than as a warning banner (23.02.03:33,49,66; 23.06.03:37; 23.01.04:61), and the blocking chain is traced upstream to its causes.
Re-pointed open questions state why the previously named stage cannot take them and which canonical row to collect them with, which is materially better tracking hygiene than a bare deferral target.
